# Prepare for and complete an external financial audit

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When an audit is required by law, a financing agreement or a voluntary stakeholder decision. Approved financial statements and the auditor's issued report, with findings assigned to remediation owners.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Agree audit applicability, scope and independence

human · human approval required


Finance leadership and qualified advisers determine the required reporting framework, periods and engagement type. Select an appropriately qualified independent auditor and confirm access, timetable and responsibilities.

- Sources: [FRC small and medium-sized enterprises](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/smes/) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Prepare reconciled financial statements and schedules

agent-runnable


Close the relevant periods and assemble trial balances, bank reconciliations, revenue, payroll, equity, debt and tax support. Label estimates and reconcile inconsistencies before supplying the controlled audit workspace.

- Sources: [FRC small and medium-sized enterprises](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/smes/) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Manage the evidence request register

agent-runnable


Track each auditor request, owner, source version and response date. Share only authorized information and preserve the provenance of evidence instead of altering records to match an expected result.

- Sources: [FRC small and medium-sized enterprises](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/smes/) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Resolve findings and approve management representations

human · human approval required


Management and the auditor discuss proposed adjustments, control issues and unresolved evidence. Authorized management approves corrections and representations; an agent does not provide audit assurance or sign on management's behalf.

- Sources: [FRC small and medium-sized enterprises](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/smes/) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Finalize the report and remediation plan

human · human approval required


Confirm that the issued statements and report match the approved versions. Distribute them only to authorized recipients and assign findings, filing obligations and the next audit-preparation cycle.

- Verify: Approved financial statements and the auditor's issued report, with findings assigned to remediation owners.
- Sources: [FRC small and medium-sized enterprises](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/smes/) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)
